questions.q: Which Data Cloud object types can CRM Analytics query, as described in this lesson?
options: Only calculated insights
Only segments
Only Tableau workbooks
Data lake objects, data model objects, and calculated insights
questions.explain: The three object types match the chapter's data flow: raw DLOs, the mapped DMOs, and pre-aggregated calculated insights.

questions.q: What is the main trade-off of querying Data Cloud live from a CRM Analytics dashboard?
options: It always copies data twice
The data is current without a copy, but the source may not be optimized for interactive dashboard queries
It is faster than any dataset in every case
It requires no permissions at all
questions.explain: Live queries avoid copies and stay current, but heavy raw-object queries can slow a dashboard and load the source.

questions.q: For a live dashboard that needs aggregate numbers, which Data Cloud object should you generally prefer?
options: A raw data lake object
An unmapped field
A calculated insight
A source system table outside Salesforce
questions.explain: Calculated insights are already aggregated, so they are much cheaper to query than scanning raw objects on every dashboard click.

questions.q: When is extracting data into a CRM Analytics dataset through a recipe the better choice?
options: When you need speed, heavy interactivity, or joins with other datasets
When you never want to transform the data
When the source cannot be reached at all
When you want to skip identity resolution
questions.explain: A dataset is a copy optimized for CRM Analytics, which suits performance-sensitive dashboards and complex joins.

questions.q: Why does this lesson advise confirming setup details in current release notes?
options: Because CRM Analytics no longer exists
Because Data Cloud cannot connect to anything
Because product names and connection options have changed several times recently
Because release notes replace all Trailhead content
questions.explain: Data Cloud was rebranded Data 360 and features shift between releases, so specifics should be verified against current documentation.
